subject: Term tilt & burst credit opportunity — renewal health & risk matrix
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@quantumpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Ruiz <emma@quantumpay.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — usage spike & early intake

Ben —

Quick note ahead of our August renewal: we saw another usage spike in May and I want to get ahead of capacity/term decisions. Topline: May token spend was ~238M (up 47% vs Apr), peak 5-minute qps doubled on two mid-month bursts. App performance held up but our infra team is nervous about sustained spend if we keep current commit.

Can you help with a short health read: 1) what portion of the increase looks steady vs bursty, 2) whether there are immediate ops levers (batching/cache) that will materially change unit economics, and 3) whether you can propose 1–2 renewal structures (term/commit + optional burst credits) that reduce rollover risk but keep price predictable.

I attached May usage export. We can loop in the infra leads if needed — Emma is on cc.

Thanks,
Carlos
Head of Platform Engineering
QuantumPay

Attachment: qpay_monthly_usage_May2027.csv (csv, 62KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@quantumpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — usage spike & early intake

Carlos — thanks for the data, this is great context. Quick summary after a rapid pass (attached slide & export):

- May overview: total tokens 238,140,000; 72% user-facing generation, 18% embeddings, 10% background reranks.
- Spike characterization: ~60% of the week-over-week growth appears burst-driven (ad hoc batch jobs + A/B test rollout on 5/11 and 5/19). The sustained baseline (median daily) increased ~12%.
- Cost/latency: average median token latency 110ms; tail (95th) 340ms during spikes — systems healthy but less headroom for concurrent traffic.

Proposed options (cleanly modeled for finance):
A) Conservative extension — 0% price change, 20% commit uplift (12 months). Covers baseline + headroom.
B) Term-tilt (recommended) — 9-month core commit sized to baseline + 10% buffer + 50M burst credit pooled for unpredictable peaks. Pricing: blended -3% vs current list on the committed tranche.
C) Aggressive discount — 24-month commit with 40% uplift, lower unit price (-9%), but longer lock-in and larger dropout risk if the test campaigns fail.

Operational levers (quick wins):
- Enable KV prefix caching for top-10 prompts (expect ~6–10% token reduction).
- Turn on async batching on non-interactive embedding ingestion (expect up to 12% cost reduction).
- Short-term canary of model variant with quantized weights for background jobs (low-latency penalty, up to 18% token-cost savings on those calls).

Risk matrix (high level):
- Business risk: medium — unclear whether the A/B tests will be sustained.
- Financial risk: medium-high if no burst coverage (overages possible).
- Operational: low — platform latency acceptable but needs runway.

Next steps I propose: 1) quick 30-min sync to confirm preferred option, 2) we ingest one-week rolling telemetry into Redwood Console so we can simulate commit sensitivity, 3) we stage KV caching change as a 2-week canary.

I attached the modeling spreadsheet with scenario P&L and a short slide that summarizes the risk/ops suggestions. Sean can help with the canary plan. Are you available Thu 17th or Fri 18th (PDT)?

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Schedule: calendly.com/ben-redwood/30m

Attachments: redwood_term_tilt_pricing_v2.xlsx; qpay_usage_may-2027-annotated.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@quantumpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 08:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — usage spike & early intake

Carlos — adding a couple of CS/ops notes on the options Ben laid out.

Operational impact & effort estimate:
- KV prefix caching: ~3 days infra effort, low risk. Will target top 25 prompts and roll via feature flags. Expected 6–8% effective token reduction for interactive flows.
- Async batching for ingestion: requires small client change and 1 day server-side config; estimate 1–2% latency impact but 10–12% cost improvement for those paths.
- Quantized background variant: ops cost to onboard ~1 week; can be limited to nightly jobs.

Pricing delta (illustrative):
- Term-tilt (9m + 50M burst credit): effective blended unit cost ~$0.00112 per 1k tokens on committed tranche (vs $0.00115 today). Burst credit consumed at the list rate then trued-up against commitment.

I'd recommend the Term-tilt for two reasons: it gives you short horizon flexibility (9m) while buying predictability for next 6–9 months via burst credit, and it leaves room to convert to a longer commit if baseline proves durable.

I've attached a short SLA-delta doc that shows response and burst handling guarantees under the tilt proposal. If you want, Sean and I can run the KV caching canary next week and share the first 72-hour telemetry.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachment: sla-delta-proposal.pdf

From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@quantumpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Emma Ruiz <emma@quantumpay.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — usage spike & early intake

Thanks Ben/Marissa — this is exactly the kind of pragmatic plan we wanted.

We’ll take Option B (Term-tilt) as the starting point: 9m commit + 50M pooled burst credit. Please mark the burst credit as a temporary buffer that we can convert into committed tokens if the pattern persists. Emma and I will confirm final dollar amounts in the deal doc, but we’re aligned on structure.

Quick ask before we lock: can Sean run the KV caching canary starting Monday (6/21) and share 72hr telemetry? If results look like your estimate we’ll fold in the expected savings into the final commit number. Also, we can take the 30-min sync on Mon 6/21 10:00am PDT.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—
Carlos
Head of Platform Engineering — QuantumPay
